text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- U.S. President Bill Clinton to offer Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a peace plan.
- Palestinians favour bombings over peace process -- poll.
- Taiba soccer player dies during match.
- Book fair no longer just "family affair".
HAARETZ
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright in tough talk with Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai: Freeze the Jewish settlement construction on Har Homa.
- Labour party leader Shimon Peres after Tel Aviv peace rally: "I felt as if I was speaking also in the name of the late Yitzhak Rabin".
- Notations to be made about undercover soldiers who killed a Palestinian from Hizme village while training.
- Heads of Israeli security industries back proposal to fuse into one corporation.
MAARIV
- Clinton to Netanyahu: No more unilateral steps.
- Israel's police present recommendations to prosecutors today on government's Bar-On affair.
- National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon goes this month to Moscow to discuss a natural gas deal for Israel.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH

- Netanyahu to tell Clinton: A final-status agreement is needed now. Source close to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat: After Netanyahu will see blood in the streets he will understand Israeli security is in our hands.
- Finance Minister Dan Meridor heads for United States, will try to draw foreign investment in Israel.
- Expectation: March cost-of-living index to be 0.6 to 0.7 percent.
